title: Active Line of Treatment Disputed in Day-Care Laparoscopy
citation: IRDAI Master Circular 2024 Clause 19.3 & Ombudsman Mumbai Order 2024/MUM/882
ruling_summary: Insurers cannot arbitrarily categorize laparoscopic surgery as non-emergency or OPD-manageable when acute surgical intervention is indicated by treating physician with elevated inflammatory markers.
legal_argument_template: The repudiation under clause 'Not Medically Necessary' is legally unsustainable. Under IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance (Clause 19.3), clinical judgment of the registered treating surgeon takes legal precedence over desk assessor determinations when operative findings confirm pathology. The patient exhibited acute symptoms requiring general anesthesia and surgical resection.

title: Unsubstantiated Pre-Existing Disease (PED) Allegation
citation: Supreme Court Ruling: Manmohan Nanda vs United India Insurance & IRDAI Reg 11
ruling_summary: The burden of proving a pre-existing condition rests entirely on the insurer with documentary clinical evidence preceding the policy inception date. Casual mentions or first-time diagnosis during hospitalization cannot be presumed pre-existing.
legal_argument_template: Under the landmark Supreme Court judgment (Civil Appeal No. 8386/2015), the onus of proving non-disclosure of PED is strictly upon the insurer through documentary evidence prior to policy inception. Diagnostic findings during current admission represent acute exacerbation and not pre-policy knowledge.

title: Rejection of Inpatient Stay for Dengue Thrombocytopenia
citation: IRDAI Circular No. IRDAI/HLT/REG/CIR/193/07/2020 & Delhi Ombudsman Ruling 2024/DEL/104
ruling_summary: Inpatient admission is clinically mandatory when platelet counts drop below 50,000/mcL or when hemorrhagic warning signs are present, superseding standard day-care exclusions.
legal_argument_template: The patient presented with NS1 positive Dengue with rapid platelet decline to <42,000/mcL, placing them at acute risk of hemorrhagic shock. IRDAI clinical admission protocol mandates continuous vital monitoring and IV fluid resuscitation for platelet counts <50,000/mcL.

title: Arbitrary Room Rent Proportionate Deduction Overcharge
citation: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) Order RP/2841/2019
ruling_summary: Proportionate deductions are applicable strictly to associated room tariff services, and cannot be proportionally deducted from medicines, surgical implants, or fixed package consumable tariffs.
legal_argument_template: The TPA has erroneously applied proportionate deductions across fixed medical consumables and surgical implant invoices. Under NCDRC precedent, proportionate reduction is confined solely to room-rent linked fees and does not extend to non-tariff medical devices or standard pharmacy billing.

title: Repudiation Due to Missing Pre-Operative Indoor Case Sheet Signature
citation: IRDAI Guidelines on Standardisation of Health Insurance Claims (Section IV)
ruling_summary: Procedural omissions such as counter-signatures cannot invalidate substantive medical care verified by billing records, diagnostic radiology, and patient discharge signatures.
legal_argument_template: We enclose the verified counter-signed indoor case record along with the treating doctor's biometric confirmation. Under IRDAI standardization regulations, substantive claims cannot be repudiated solely due to procedural clarification delays if medical records corroborate treatment.
